subject: Control handshake surge during staged upgrade - Medigent
messages:
From: Samantha Clark <samantha.clark@medigent.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: infraops@medigent.com
Date: 2026-11-29T01:45:00Z
Subject: Control plane re-handshakes during tonight's private cluster upgrade

Hi Priyom,

We started the staged upgrade on our private VPC cluster at 01:20 UTC and are seeing repeated control-plane re-handshakes and short disconnects across 4 of our nodes. Around 01:23-01:40 UTC we observed 5-10s API latency spikes and intermittent 502s for our inference traffic.

Attached is a small collection of controller logs and a short timeline we captured. The symptoms look similar to a KV cache divergence we saw last year (we've included that reference in the timeline) but the timing aligns tightly with the agent rollout window. Can you confirm whether any change in handshake/resync behavior was pushed from Redwood during your upgrade canary at that time?

This is impacting a production subset of traffic (non-critical but customer-facing). We need an initial triage and suggested mitigation so we can decide whether to pause the rollout.

Attachments: controlplane-logs-20261129.tar.gz (18MB), upgrade-timeline-medigent-20261129.pdf

Thanks,
Samantha Clark
Head of Infrastructure, Medigent Health
Samantha.Clark@medigent.com

Thanks — we captured a dump and the manifest; attaching both. The timeline PDF includes the rollout window and the node ordering. Observations from our side:
- Handshake flurries start ~20s after the first canary agent is upgraded.
- Client-side (our agents) saw a short-lived KV cache mismatch error for 2 requests; service recovered after resync but subsequent requests hit 502 briefly.
- No obvious kernel-level connectivity issues from the host.

Attachments: controlplane-logs-20261129.tar.gz, upgrade-timeline-medigent-20261129.pdf, node1-tcpdump.pcap (3.2MB)

We're prepared to pause the rollout if you advise; please let us know your initial findings from the logs and whether you recommend rollback or config tweak.

—Samantha

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Clark <samantha.clark@medigent.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T10:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Control plane re-handshakes during tonight's private cluster upgrade

Hi Samantha — thanks for the additional artifacts and for standing by for the bridge. We completed an initial triage and here are our findings and recommended next steps: 

Initial findings (summary):
- The controlplane logs show a spike of TLS re-handshake events correlated with the agent process restart sequence in the canary. The handshakes themselves succeeded, but our control mux experienced a short window where sessions were reallocated which triggered transient 502s for some in-flight requests.
- The tcpdump indicates a small burst of duplicate SYNs and session resets during the agent upgrade sequence which aligns with a known timing sensitivity in our connection rebalancer under certain concurrency profiles.
- No evidence of persistent KV cache corruption; cache checksums re-synced successfully in all cases. The short-lived mismatch Samantha observed is consistent with the resync window we see during session reallocation.

Immediate mitigations we recommend:
1) Pause the rollout to the remaining nodes (Medigent ops to confirm).
2) Apply a temporary handshake-throttling patch on the canary control mux (we can push a non-disruptive config flip that spaces reconnect backoffs) — Marcus will coordinate.
3) If rolling traffic must remain live, route the affected traffic to your warm standby pool for the next 2 hours while we validate the patch on the canary.

Next steps and deliverables:
- Marcus will provide the patch diff and short runbook (JIRA: JIRA-SUP-1247) by EOD UTC.
- Grace will run a targeted canary validation with your infra team and report behavioral metrics at 3:30 UTC.
- Redwood will deliver a short RCA within 72 hours including logs, timeline, and the proposed long-term fix to make the rebalancer resilient to this concurrency profile.

Evidence artifacts we will include in the RCA: controller logs, agent side traces, tcpdump excerpts, and the canary patch diff. We've uploaded a working folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMEDIGENT-ops (access granted to your infra group).

Please confirm you want us to hold the rollout and whether you want us to apply the handshake-throttling patch to the canary now or after we've validated on a separate staging canary.

Thanks again for the quick artifacts — we know this impacts traffic and appreciate the rapid collaboration.

Best,
